senses.sense_definition: An outline, boundary, or surface border, especially one representing a curving form or shape.

examples.text: The artist carefully traced the smooth <w>contour</w> of the dancer's back.
The sleek <w>contour</w> of the new sports car reduces wind resistance at high speeds.

senses.sense_definition: A line on a map connecting points of equal height above sea level.

examples.text: The steep hill is shown by closely spaced <w>contours</w> on the hiking map.
Before starting our trek, we checked every <w>contour</w> on the map to avoid dangerous terrain.

senses.sense_definition: The general features, outline, or main points of a situation, plan, or debate.

examples.text: The negotiators have established the broad <w>contours</w> of a peace agreement.
Her lecture focused on the changing <w>contours</w> of European foreign policy after the war.

senses.sense_definition: A single speech segment that undergoes an internal transition between differing phonetic qualities.

examples.text: Affricates and diphthongs are typical examples of a phonetic <w>contour</w> segment.
The phonologist analyzed the pitch <w>contour</w> across the tone language dialect.

senses.sense_definition: To apply cosmetics to the face to create shadow effects and enhance bone structure.

examples.text: She watched an online tutorial to learn how to <w>contour</w> her cheekbones effectively.

senses.sense_definition: To shape or form something so that it follows a curved outline or surface.

examples.text: The ergonomic chair is designed to <w>contour</w> to the natural shape of the spine.
The foam mattress <w>contours</w> around your body to provide maximum comfort during sleep.

senses.sense_definition: To mark a topographical map or chart with lines indicating equal elevation.

examples.text: The surveyor used satellite data to <w>contour</w> the mountainous area accurately.
Modern software can <w>contour</w> rugged terrain in minutes using high-resolution drone scans.

senses.sense_definition: To mold, influence, or shape the general course, conditions, or boundaries of something.

examples.text: Economic anxieties will likely <w>contour</w> public debate over the coming decades.
The outcome of the international summit will <w>contour</w> environmental policy for years to come.
